Uluslararası Ticaretin Ekonomi Politiği ve 1980’den Günümüze Türkiye Dış Ticaretinde Yaşanan Dönüşüm
journal: Bulletin of Economic Theory and Analysis
abstract: Uluslararası ticaret, küresel ekonomik gelişmenin temel bir itici gücü olarak kabul edilmekte, ulusal ekonomilerin genişlemesini kolaylaştırmakta ve ülkelerin kapitalist dünya sistemine entegrasyonunu şekillendirmektedir. Bu çalışma, 1980 sonrası Türkiye ekonomisinde ihracata dayalı büyüme stratejisinin gerçek performansını dış ticaret miktar ve fiyat endeksleri ile ticaret hadleri üzerinden incelemektedir. Çalışmanın temel argümanı, ihracat hacmindeki artışın tek başına kalkınma göstergesi olmadığı; aksine, ithal girdi bağımlılığı ve fiyat yapısındaki bozulmalar nedeniyle Türkiye’nin uluslararası ticarette yapısal bir dezavantajla karşı karşıya olduğudur. İthalat ve ihracat miktar endekslerinin birlikte yükselmesi, üretim yapısının dış girdiye bağımlı biçimde genişlediğini göstermektedir. Bu durum, brüt ihracat artışının net katma değer artışı anlamına gelmediğini ortaya koymaktadır. Öte yandan, özellikle 2010 sonrası dönemde ticaret hadlerinde gözlenen kalıcı gerileme, Türkiye’nin aynı miktarda ithalat için daha fazla ihracat yapmak zorunda kaldığını ve dış ticaret yoluyla örtük bir reel gelir kaybı yaşandığını göstermektedir. Bulgular, ihracata dayalı büyüme modelinin teknoloji yoğun ve yüksek katma değerli bir dönüşüm yaratamadığını, aksine küresel tedarik zincirlerine düşük katma değerli eklemlenme biçimini pekiştirdiğini ortaya koymaktadır. Çalışmada, dış ticaret genişlemesinin yapısal bağımlılık ilişkilerini yeniden üreten bir dinamik taşıdığı ileri sürülmektedir.

title: Trading privacy for personalisation: Ethical trust and high school students’ intention to use AI in education
journal: International Journal of Business and Management (IJBM)
abstract: Educational AI tools personalise learning by drawing on sensitive student data, yet the privacy calculus assumes that people can freely weigh benefits against risks and decline when risks dominate. This assumption is doubtful for adolescents, who have limited ability to scrutinise institutional data practices and little scope to opt out when AI is embedded in schooling. This study examines how perceived personalisation benefits, perceived data sensitivity and privacy concerns relate to high school students’ intention to use AI, and tests whether ethical trust, defined as confidence that an AI system will handle personal data responsibly, transparently and in the user’s interest, links privacy concerns to intention. Survey data from 323 students across IB, A Level, CBSE, American and other curriculums were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Perceived benefits strongly predicted ethical trust (β = .605, p < .001) and intention to use AI directly (β = .454, p < .001). Perceived data sensitivity raised privacy concerns (β = .563, p < .001), and privacy concerns modestly reduced ethical trust (β of negative .185, p = .002). Ethical trust in turn predicted intention to use AI (β = .453, p < .001), whereas the direct effect of privacy concerns on intention was negligible (β = .023, p = .507). The model explained 65.9% of the variance in intention. The pattern indicates that privacy concern shapes adoption through eroded trust rather than through avoidance, and that usefulness can build trust without proof of trustworthy data practices. Limitations include the cross sectional design, self reported intentions and weaker measurement of data sensitivity. Schools and providers should therefore demonstrate responsible data governance rather than simply reassure students.

title: The sustainable development goals and Aldo Leopold’s land ethic: A philosophical analysis of ecological sustainability, human well-being, and environmental ethics
journal: International Journal of Business and Management (IJBM)
abstract: Aldo Leopold’s Land Ethic is one of the seminal works in environmental ethics because he brought the consideration of ethics from human interests to the biotic community. The idea of ecological integrity, stability and beauty, however, suggests a philosophical question about the relationship between ecological responsibilities and human health, justice and democratic choice. This article looks at how the norms of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) can be applied to Leopold’s Land Ethic in a constructive way. The study collates Leopold’s original formulation, philosophical understandings of ecological holism, and sustainable development, human rights and environmental justice literature with the use of structured secondary-literature review and reported with reference to the PRISMA 2020 framework. The analysis in particular emphasizes SDG 15 (Life on Land), SDG 13 (Climate Action), SDG 1 (No Poverty), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities) and SDG 16 (Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions). The article suggests that the Land Ethic and SDGs can be engaged productively when ecological integrity becomes a state of human long-term flourishing, not an excuse to ignore social justice or human dignity. The SDG framework brings in practical elements such as poverty alleviation, equality, participation, institutional accountability and intergenerational responsibility that could reinforce the modern ethical understanding of Leopold’s ecological vision. The article ends by suggesting that a pluralist interpretation of the Land Ethic can be used to establish an integrated vision of ecological and social justice, where ecological conservation and human welfare are seen as interconnected with intergenerational responsibilities.

title: The role of chronic hypoxemia and systemic inflammation in attentional impairment among miners with COPD of occupational origin
abstract: Abstract Background The systemic manifestations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) are well established, but associations among systemic inflammation, pulmonary function, arterial oxygenation, and attention remain insufficiently characterized in coal miners. Methods This comparative cross-sectional study included 180 male underground coal miners: 90 with occupational COPD and 90 coal-dust-exposed miners without COPD. COPD was staged as GOLD 1–4; all COPD participants had a mixed chronic bronchitic–emphysematous phenotype, and pneumoconiosis and other interstitial lung diseases were excluded radiologically. CRP, total cholesterol, post-bronchodilator FEV₁, PaO₂, and selective attention using the Münsterberg test were assessed. Correlations were examined by group, and adjusted regression, hypoxemia-stratified, and exploratory ROC analyses were conducted within COPD. Results Compared with miners without COPD, the pooled COPD group had higher CRP (2.3 ± 2.5 vs. 0.9 ± 1.4 mg/L) and cholesterol (4.9 ± 0.9 vs. 4.4 ± 0.9 mmol/L), lower FEV₁ (56.0 ± 16.1% vs. 111.8 ± 13.9% predicted) and PaO₂ (64.3 ± 5.5 vs. 82.6 ± 5.2 mmHg; all P < 0.001), and lower attention scores (15.6 ± 4.1 vs. 17.3 ± 4.7 points; P = 0.007). Within COPD, attention correlated with PaO₂ (rₛ = 0.75; P < 0.00001), and participants with PaO₂ < 60 mmHg had lower scores than those with PaO₂ 60–79 mmHg (12.5 ± 3.4 vs. 16.4 ± 3.8; P < 0.001). PaO₂ was the only independently associated variable in the adjusted model (B = 0.528 points/mmHg; 95% CI, 0.406–0.650; P < 0.001). Exploratory discrimination was good (AUC = 0.878; 95% bootstrap CI, 0.762–0.961), but was not externally validated. Conclusions In this cross-sectional occupational sample, lower arterial oxygenation was the most consistent correlate of poorer selective attention among miners with occupational COPD. The observed relationships with CRP, cholesterol, airflow obstruction, and work experience are compatible with the proposed occupational–inflammatory–respiratory framework-decreased attention, but do not establish temporal sequence, mediation, or causality.

title: The Relationship Between Approval of Nursing Actions and Patient Satisfaction Levels In The Inpatient Ward of Bougenville 3, Dr. Loekmono Hadi Kudus Regional Hospital
journal: International Journal of Science and Environment (IJSE)
abstract: Consent for nursing actions is an important part of patient-centered care because it plays a role in improving communication, trust, and patient satisfaction. This study aims to analyze the relationship between consent for nursing actions and patient satisfaction levels in the Inpatient Room of Bougenville 3, Dr. Loekmono Hadi Kudus Regional General Hospital. This study used a quantitative correlation analytic design with a cross-sectional approach. The study population was 53 inpatients, with a sample of 47 respondents selected using a purposive sampling technique. Data were collected using the Quality of Informed Consent (QuIC) instrument and the Patient Satisfaction Questionnaire Short Form (PSQ-18). Data analysis was performed univariately and bivariately using the Spearman Rank correlation test with a significance level of 0.05. The results showed that 63.8% of respondents received consent for nursing actions in the good category and 59.6% had a very satisfied level of satisfaction. The Spearman Rank test showed a significant relationship between consent for nursing actions and patient satisfaction (p = 0.000; r = 0.919), indicating a very strong positive relationship. It was concluded that the implementation of improved nursing action agreements contributed to increasing patient satisfaction and therefore needed to be maintained and improved as part of efforts to improve the quality of nursing services.
